label: Design 3 - Office-Side Service Rooms + Bright Service-End Day Room
summary: A less extreme but still structural option: sacrifice the office to make separated laundry/WC/bathroom service rooms, then turn the bright laundry/entrance/toilet end into a useful day room or back-entry sitting zone.
room_changes: Bedroom 2 stays as the teenage bedroom for this version.
The office is largely absorbed into separated adjacent bathroom, laundry, WC, and storage rooms.
The current laundry/toilet/entrance area becomes a bright day room, study nook, or back-entry sitting space.
The current lounge becomes a more deliberate evening media room.
The sunroom is retained, upgraded, or removed in a later stage.
daylight_strategy: Recover useful light from the current laundry/toilet area without immediately needing a new bedroom.
Give the family a small bright daytime sitting or reading zone near the real back arrival.
Keep the sunroom comfort problem visible as a later-stage issue rather than pretending it is solved.
movement_strategy: Make the back entry feel more welcoming and less like entering through service rooms.
Improve bathroom, laundry, and WC logic for the three residents and visitors.
Preserve Bedroom 2 privacy while adding a better-used light zone nearby.
build_scope: Replan the office and bathroom side as separated service rooms for bathroom, laundry, WC, and storage.
Move or replace laundry and WC services.
Alter walls and doors around the office, bathroom, laundry, and entrance.
Refinish the released service area as a day room or back-entry sitting space.
risks: Losing the office removes a valuable enclosed quiet room.
The service-room cluster could make the central hallway feel tight if not designed carefully.
It improves light use but may not fully solve the main lounge problem.
A replacement quiet/work room needs to be deliberately planned.
cost_notes: Broad planning band: NZD 140k to 280k+ depending on drainage, waterproofing, and wall changes.
